event.title: Open Lab Hours at AI Center for Civic and Social Good
event.room_number: Room 125, AI Center for Civic and Social Good
event.address: 150 E San Fernando St, San Jose, CA 95112
event.description:
Drop in, explore, and create! During Open Lab Hours, SJSU students, faculty, staff, and SJPL library members are welcome to discover cutting-edge AI tools, experiment with new technologies, and bring their ideas to life.

Whether you're working on a class assignment, building a passion project, supporting your community, or simply curious about AI, we've got the resources to help you get started.

What you'll find:
• State-of-the-art computers and powerful AI software
• Responsible AI tools for academic, public service, and community projects
• Collaborative workspaces for individuals and small groups
• Open access for anyone with a valid SJSU Tower Card or SJPL Library Card

Come learn, create, collaborate, and see what's possible with AI!

event.title: What Makes AI Scary? A dialogue event for SJSU students
event.description:
Are you haunted by the specter of computers with super-human intelligence who might not wish humans well? Worried that ChatGPT might be a monkeypaw granting wishes that turn out to be cursed?  Scared that you're the only SJSU student who feels the way you do about AI products (no mattter how that is you're feeling)?

Join us to explore the things that makes AI scary while you learn how to engage in dialogue (not debate) with other SJSU students.  Whatever your feelings about AI, your voice is welcome in this dialogue!

Please RSVP at https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScsBlcEpCFUD1QlU6VvIzCjojFN5tSpdGpcQG6vBZeEg3tbKw/viewform?usp=header

Questions? Email Janet Stemwedel (janet.stemwedel@sjsu.edu)

Supported by a College of Humanities & the Arts Aristic Excellence Programming Grant

data.title: Condensed Matter Seminar with Archana Raja: Quantum Materials in the Age of AI: From 2D Heterostructures to Agentic Discovery
data.summary: Understanding and controlling quantum phases of matter is one of the central challenges of condensed matter physics. In this talk, I will describe how our group uses this challenge as a unifying thread to connect experiment, theory, and artificial intelligence, with topological van der Waals materials as our primary arena.
